Using the frozen breeder point (plasma current I_p = 9.66 MA, centrepost field 16.84 T, negative triangularity delta = -0.30, validated in nonlinear CGYRO), we checked the modeled confinement time against com…

headline: Startup Modeled End to End, Cold Plasma to the Frozen Point
summary: In the digital twin we ran the full startup sequence for the breeder: current ramp to I_p = 9.66 MA, field ramp to the 16.84 T centrepost point, shaping to delta = -0.30, and checked the path against the frozen design point (Q = 3.076, P_fus = 85.04 MW).

headline: Shutdown and Ramp-Down Modeled Without a Forced Disruption
summary: We modeled the reverse of the startup path, ramping plasma current down from I_p = 9.66 MA and the centrepost field down from 16.84 T, checking every step against the structural margin already validated for the centrepost (181 MPa, PASS).

summary: The operating window is the region in current, field, and shaping space bounded by structural, confinement, and stability limits together, not any one alone.

headline: Radial Build Analysis Finds ~2 cm of Recoverable Margin
summary: The radial build is the stack of layer thicknesses (centrepost, shield, blanket, vessel, magnet case) from the machine axis outward; each layer's minimum is set by a structural or shielding requirement.

headline: Neutron-Activation Profile Computed for the Breeder's First Wall
summary: Material activation follows accumulated dpa/appm under neutron flux, and for a D-T machine that flux is dominated by 14.1 MeV neutrons from the fusion reaction itself.

Starting from the computed activation profile of the breeder's neutron-facing structure (first-wall- and shield-peaked, under the 14.1 MeV D-T neutron spectrum), we estimated where the resulting material fall…

headline: Thermal Gradient Managed Across a 1,000-Kelvin-Plus Span
summary: The machine's thermal balance spans the ~20 K REBCO cryogenic network at one end and plasma-facing surfaces exposed to fusion power (P_fus = 85.04 MW at the frozen point) at the other: a gradient of well over a thousand kelvin across a few meters of structure.

headline: Fuel-Cycle Inventory Balanced Against Losses and Decay
summary: Net tritium available equals production minus operating losses minus radioactive decay (tritium half-life 12.3 yr) minus the startup inventory reserved for the next machine.

headline: Tritium Retention in the First Wall, Bounded
summary: Not all bred tritium makes it to the fuel-cycle loop; some stays trapped in first-wall material, a function of material choice, temperature, and 14.1 MeV neutron fluence.

headline: Blanket Breeding Uniformity Checked Across Near-4π Coverage
summary: Closing net breeding above unity depends on coverage near 4pi around the plasma, not just an average multiplication factor: TBR = (int_V Sigma_T phi dV) / R_fus. A cold spot in coverage can undercut an otherwise-adequate average.

headline: Plasma-Facing Material Checked Against Combined Design Loads
summary: Plasma-facing material survivability depends jointly on 14.1 MeV neutron fluence (dpa/appm accumulation) and the thermal load carried at the frozen power point (P_fus = 85.04 MW), not on either load checked in isolation. We ran a candidate plasma-facing material against both loads together in the modeled environment.

headline: One gate scoped and left open, on the record: helium-3 doesn't close indigenously
summary: One gate scoped and left open, on the record: helium-3 doesn't close indigenously.

headline: MHD Operating Limit Located — With the β_N Caveat Named
summary: The MHD stability boundary bounds how much plasma pressure the shaping and current profile can support before instability threatens the discharge, a Troyon-style normalized-beta (beta_N) limit.

headline: Disruption Load on Structure Bounded Within Existing Margin
summary: A disruption or vertical-displacement event dumps plasma current and thermal energy into the vessel and centrepost on a fast timescale, the structural case that has to survive even when the plasma doesn't.

headline: Control Policy Validated in the Twin Before It Touches Hardware
summary: A control policy tuned against a digital twin can be checked for safety and performance before it ever runs near real plasma; the twin stands in for the machine, cheaply and repeatedly, until the policy's behavior is understood.

headline: Twin Reproduces the Frozen Design Point Against Independent Codes
summary: A digital twin earns trust by matching independent physics codes at the same operating point, not just by matching itself. We benchmarked the twin's output against the CGYRO turbulence dataset and the frozen design-point anchors: Q = 3.076, P_fus = 85.04 MW, I_p = 9.66 MA, centrepost field 16.84 T.

headline: Reproduction Confirmed on a Third Independent Environment
summary: A result only counts as reproducible if someone outside the team, on a different machine, gets the same number from the same published inputs. The AI + Quantum method deposit was built for exactly this test, and it has now been re-run cold on an independent environment beyond the ones used at deposit time.

headline: Sensitivity Analysis Narrows What Actually Moves the Design Point
summary: A design-point sensitivity study ranks input parameters by how much each one shifts the output (Q, P_fus, TBR) when varied, separating what matters from what doesn't.

headline: A Prior Assumption Revised on New Modeling Evidence
summary: A design register only stays honest if assumptions move when the evidence does; otherwise 'canonical' just means 'first guess, never revisited.' One input assumption behind the current anchor set was revised this cycle after new modeling evidence came in; the revision is now reflected in the canonical anchors this feed…

headline: An Open Gate, Named Before It Bites: He-3 Doesn't Close Indigenously
summary: A materials platform's engineering depends on which by-products stand on their own and which are strategic value that doesn't yet close a supply chain.

headline: A Result That Didn't Clear, Reported Honestly
summary: The beta_N comparison between the modeled operating point and the reference stability limit is a straightforward ratio, and this cycle it did not resolve in our favor. The comparison stands at 2.13 vs. 1.53, unresolved, and we are not rounding it into a pass or burying it under a more favorable anchor.

headline: Cross-Check Between Breeder and Burner Assumptions Holds
summary: The breeder (Hyperion, a D-T spherical tokamak) and the burner (Aegis / MetroVolt, a D-3He tandem mirror) are different machines, but they share underlying assumptions (REBCO conductor behavior, cryogenic architecture, structural methodology) and those shared assumptions have to stay consistent across both programs' an…

headline: Breeding Blanket Design Paper Published
summary: It covers blanket geometry, neutron multiplication, and coverage fraction: the three levers that turn a fusion neutron into a bred tritium atom. Governing form: TBR = (integral of Sigma_T phi dV) / R_fus.

headline: Net Self-Sufficiency Case Published as a Standalone Paper
summary: Hyperion's net tritium breeding result now has its own standalone paper, separate from the blanket design it draws on.

headline: NV Sensing: An Honest Gap Named, Not a Multiplier Claimed
key_anchor: NV 0.189 pT/√Hz @125 kHz (gated) ; NV neutron tol ~39× short (open)
summary: Magnetometer sensitivity and radiation tolerance are two different specifications; a device can improve on one while falling short on the other. The number we're naming today, plainly: the NV-diamond sensing package's neutron tolerance for in-vessel deployment sits roughly 39x short of the qualification target.

headline: Net Tritium Breeding Margin by Divertor Configuration: 1.12 SN / 1.07 DN
summary: Net breeding above unity requires a neutron multiplier (an (n,2n) reaction) and coverage near 4pi, with margin held back to cover losses, tritium decay (half-life 12.3 yr), and the startup inventory the next machine will need: TBR = (int_V Sigma_T phi dV) / R_fus, via 6Li(n,alpha)T (+4.78 MeV, thermal) and 7Li(n,n'alph…

headline: Transport: modeling the edge and scrape-off layer
summary: The scrape-off layer — the thin region between the confined core and the divertor where field lines intersect material surfaces — governs how much heat and particle flux actually reaches the first wall and divertor targets, versus how much is spread or radiated away first.

headline: Negative-Triangularity Shaping Paper Published
summary: Triangularity is defined geometrically: delta = (R0 - R_X) / a. At the frozen design point delta ~ -0.30 - negative, meaning the boundary points the opposite way from a conventional tokamak.

headline: Center-Stack Shielding and Engineering Paper Published
summary: The hardest structural column in the machine - the center stack that carries the toroidal-field coil through the plasma core - has its shielding and engineering paper drafted and held.

headline: Magnet-Twin Fused Quench Detection Reaches AUC 0.992
summary: Fusing digital-twin state estimates with real-time magnet sensor telemetry lets a quench-detection classifier flag a pre-quench state earlier and more reliably than either source alone, measured, on the modeled/simulated test set, by the area under the ROC curve.

headline: Transport: cross-checking micro-instabilities with a second code
summary: Every major confinement claim in Kronos's public physics rests on CGYRO, the nonlinear gyrokinetic code behind the δ = −0.30 negative-triangularity result.

headline: Design locked: the control-sensor network
summary: Design lock: Kronos has locked a reference architecture for the sensor network that feeds the plasma-control system — the layout of magnetic, thermal, and quench-relevant sensing that the controller reads in real time.

headline: Five-Channel Direct Energy Conversion Paper Published
summary: The paper describing how the burner turns charged particles directly into current - no steam cycle - is drafted and held.

headline: NV-Diamond Magnetometry Reaches 0.189 pT/√Hz at 125 kHz
summary: Magnetometer sensitivity is reported as a noise floor per root-hertz at a stated frequency; the lower the number, the smaller a field change the sensor can resolve above its own noise.

headline: Control-Barrier-Function Clamp Cuts Safety Violations to 0/100
summary: A control-barrier-function (CBF) safety clamp sits between a control policy's raw output and the plasma, mathematically constraining any action that would push the modeled state outside a defined safe set; the policy acts freely inside the boundary, but the clamp refuses to let it cross out.

headline: Thermal: following the energy path to usable power
summary: The burner line converts fusion output to usable power through a fundamentally different path than a conventional thermal plant: charged-particle exhaust from the D–³He tandem-mirror core is decelerated across biased grids and collectors in a five-channel direct-energy-conversion stack — electrostatic, MHD, thermionic,…

headline: Thermal: the cold-side energy books
summary: Keeping a magnet set near 20 K — REBCO tape's operating point, which is what makes a compact, high-field centrepost buildable at all — demands continuous cryogenic cooling capacity, and every heat load into that cold system has to be accounted for: conduction through supports, radiation, current leads, and any AC losse…

headline: 20 K Cryogenic Architecture Paper Published
summary: The cold system that keeps both machines' REBCO coils superconducting has its architecture paper published and held.

headline: Vacuum Vessel Structural and Thermal Paper Published
summary: The paper covering the vacuum vessel's structural and thermal behavior - the outer shell that holds vacuum around the plasma and carries disruption loads - is drafted and held.

headline: Divertor and Exhaust Handling Paper Published
summary: Where the plasma's heat and particle exhaust actually go is the subject of a published design paper.

headline: Reliability: how long each component is expected to last
summary: Component lifetime in a fusion machine is rarely a single number — different components fail against different mechanisms on different timescales: neutron-flux-driven material degradation for the centrepost and first wall, cycle-count fatigue for superconducting joints, and straightforward wear for balance-of-plant equ…

headline: Reliability: how often the machine needs service
summary: Maintenance-interval planning follows directly from the component-lifetime analysis: once each component class has an expected service life, the machine's overall maintenance schedule is built around whichever components need attention soonest, sequenced to minimize downtime rather than servicing everything on the same…

headline: First-Wall Materials Under 14 MeV Neutrons — Paper Published
summary: The most demanding surface in the machine - the first wall facing the D-T plasma directly - has its neutron-survivability paper drafted and held.

headline: Tandem-Mirror End-Plug Physics Paper Published
summary: The physics of holding plasma pressure at the ends of a tandem mirror - rather than in a closed torus - has its own published paper.

headline: Plug-Density Operating Point Stated in the Open — Paper Published
summary: The mirror's hardest operating requirement - central-cell plug density - gets a dedicated paper, and the series states it in the open rather than folding it into a broader design document.

headline: Sensitivity: how robust is the frozen design point
summary: A frozen design point — Q = 3.076, P_fus = 85.04 MW, I_p = 9.66 MA, δ = −0.30 — is a single set of numbers, and a sensitivity analysis asks how much each input can move before the design's key outputs, chiefly Q and the TBR ≥ 1.05 breeding margin, drift outside acceptable bounds.

headline: Control robustness: rejecting disturbances during operation
summary: A control system that only performs well against the nominal, undisturbed case is not ready for a real machine — sensor noise, small field perturbations and unmodeled dynamics are present in every operating moment.

headline: Low-Neutron D–³He Reaction Economy Paper Published
summary: Why a low neutron fraction changes the entire engineering picture is the subject of a published paper.

headline: Helium-3 Co-Production Pathway Paper Published
summary: The breeder's highest-value by-product gets its own pathway paper: how Hyperion's neutron economy, run alongside its primary tritium-breeding mission, can co-produce helium-3.

headline: Neutron-Economy Materials Platform Paper Published
summary: The public case for Hyperion as a materials platform - not a power plant - is written up as its own paper, drawing the breeding, isotope, and neutron-services threads across the series into one framing document. Drafted and held.

headline: AI/ML Plasma Control Paper (KRONOS-CTRL) Published
summary: The paper positioning the control system as a first-class subsystem - not an add-on to the plasma physics - is drafted and held.

headline: Microsecond Vertical-Displacement Control Paper Published
summary: Catching a vertical-displacement event before it becomes a disruption is a timing problem as much as a physics one - the paper on microsecond-scale VDE control is drafted and held.

headline: Load-Following and Grid Integration Paper Published
summary: How the burner line tracks a real grid demand profile - rather than running at fixed output - is the subject of a published paper.

headline: Digital-Twin Architecture and Validation Paper Published
summary: The paper documenting the digital twin's architecture - a live, component-by-component model of the machine used to validate designs and train control policy before hardware exists - is drafted and held.

headline: Gyrokinetic Turbulence Paper (CGYRO) Published
summary: CGYRO is the turbulence code used to check whether the delta ~ -0.30 shaping actually raises the critical gradient for ITG/TEM edge turbulence the way the analytic argument predicts. This paper is the physics writeup around those runs - methodology, resolution, and the confinement conclusions drawn.

headline: Edge and Scrape-Off-Layer Transport Paper Published
summary: Heat and particle transport at the plasma boundary - the scrape-off layer between the confined core and the divertor - has its own published paper.

headline: MHD Stability and Operating-Limits Paper Published
summary: Where the operating window ends - the MHD stability limits that bound how hard the plasma can be pushed - is the subject of a published paper.

headline: Magnet Quench and Protection Paper Published
summary: The failure mode engineered out at the design stage - a superconducting magnet quench - has its own protection paper, drafted and held.

headline: Fuel-Cycle Staging Strategy Paper Published
summary: Why the tritium fuel cycle comes in stages, rather than all at once, is documented in a published paper.

headline: Isotope Production and Neutron-Services Paper Published
summary: The byproducts of a high-flux neutron source - the neutron-services case that sits alongside tritium breeding - have their own published paper.

headline: Medical-Isotope Pathway Paper Published
summary: The public-health application of Hyperion's neutron economy - a pathway toward medical isotope production - has its own published paper.

headline: Reproducibility and Open-Evaluator Method Paper Published
summary: The methods paper making every result in the series executable - not just citable - is drafted and held.

headline: De-Risking Register Methodology Paper Published
summary: The methodology behind turning a fusion machine into a set of checkable, individually-stamped claims - the de-risking register approach - has its own paper, drafted and held.

headline: Aegis Defense-Burner Configuration Paper Published
summary: The configuration paper for Aegis - the fixed forward-base defense housing built around the shared burner core - is drafted and held.

headline: MetroVolt Data-Center-Burner Configuration Paper Published
summary: The configuration paper for MetroVolt - the data-center housing built around the same shared burner core as Aegis - is drafted and held.

headline: Thermal Management Across the Cryo–Plasma Gradient — Paper Published
summary: Managing a temperature gradient that spans hundreds of kelvin over a short physical distance - from a ~20 K REBCO coil to a plasma core at fusion temperatures - is the subject of a published paper.

headline: Neutron Fluence and Shielding Budget for the Breeder Core — Paper Published
summary: Every 14.1 MeV D–T neutron that crosses a boundary is working life drawn against a component.

headline: Activation and Materials Lifetime Across Both Machines — Paper Published
summary: A single paper works the activation question for both machines side by side, because the two cores put very different neutron loads on their structures.

headline: First-Wall and Divertor Survivability Under Steady-State Load — Paper Published
summary: The parts that touch the plasma directly — first wall and divertor — carry this paper's subject: how they survive years of combined heat flux and neutron bombardment rather than a single pulse.

headline: Pressure Performance and the Beta Limit — Paper Published
summary: How hard the plasma can be pressurized before instabilities set the limit is the subject of this paper — the pressure-performance case that feeds the broader MHD stability work in the series.

headline: Sustaining the Plasma Current — Current-Drive Paper Published
summary: A plasma current doesn't sustain itself indefinitely without external drive, and this paper documents how Hyperion holds its current through a pulse.

headline: Feeding the Burn: Pellet Fueling Paper Published
summary: A fusion plasma consumes fuel as it burns, and keeping density in the right operating band over a pulse is a supply problem as much as a physics one.

headline: Turning Plasma Into Data: The Diagnostics Suite Paper
summary: You can't manage what the instrumentation can't see, and this paper documents the diagnostic suite built to characterize Hyperion's plasma in real time — the sensing layer everything else, including control, depends on.

headline: Proof Before the AI Touches Plasma: Control-Validation Methodology
summary: Before any learned control policy is allowed near a live plasma, it has to clear a validation methodology — and this paper documents that gate.

headline: The Modeling Stack Behind Every Design Claim — Architecture Paper
summary: Every number stated at the frozen design point traces back to a specific place in a modeling stack, and this paper documents that stack's architecture end to end — which code does which job, and how outputs from one stage feed the next.

headline: Checking Our Codes Against the Field's — Verification Paper
summary: A modeling stack is only as trustworthy as its agreement with independently-developed tools, and this paper is the verification exercise: Hyperion's own simulation results checked against established codes used across the fusion field, not just against themselves.

headline: The Safety Case for a Low-Neutron Burner — Paper Published
summary: Fusion has an inherent safety property fission doesn't: there is no chain reaction to run away, because a fusion plasma isn't self-sustaining without continuous external heating and fueling — cut either and the reaction stops on its own.

headline: What Stays Behind: Waste and Activation Profile Across the Fleet — Paper Published
summary: An honest accounting of what a fusion machine leaves behind — not just what it produces while running — is the subject of this paper, covering the waste and activation profile across both product lines rather than as an afterthought.

headline: Site-Level Environmental Characterization — Paper Published
summary: It documents the physical envelope a build occupies and the standard environmental-engineering questions that come with siting industrial equipment of this kind. The paper is scoped narrowly to characterization: what a site needs to support, physically, not an impact assessment or a regulatory filing.

headline: A Short Companion Note on Confinement and Heating
summary: Not every result needs a full paper, and this short companion note is one of those — a focused addendum to the confinement-scaling and current-drive papers, tying the two together at the point where heating method and confinement performance interact.

headline: Blanket Neutronics Dataset Documented as a Standalone Data Descriptor
summary: The descriptor's job is precise reuse: geometry, source terms, and multiplication assumptions documented well enough that the neutron-transport runs behind the blanket case can be re-derived.

headline: Turbulent-Transport Run Data Documented as a Standalone Descriptor
summary: It covers run parameters, resolution, and convergence criteria for the nonlinear CGYRO work behind δ = −0.30. Kronos is a family-owned American company.

headline: Digital-Twin Validation Data Documented as a Standalone Descriptor
summary: The discipline is the same one that runs through every simulated claim in the series: modeled and simulated results are checked, and the check itself is documented, not just asserted.

headline: Showing the Inputs, Not Just the Outputs: An Assumptions-and-Sensitivities Note
summary: A number stated without its inputs is a claim; a number stated with the assumptions and sensitivities behind it is a result someone else can check. This companion note is that practice worked as its own short document rather than buried in each paper's methods section.

headline: The Work We Haven't Closed, Named: An Open-Gates Companion Note
summary: Publishing what didn't close, alongside what did, is the harder half of an honest series, and this companion note is where that happens for the results still open at this stage. None are hidden elsewhere and restated for effect — they're named once, plainly, and left open.

headline: Power Quality at the Grid Boundary: Direct-DC Interface Paper Published
summary: Direct energy conversion changes what shows up at the boundary between the machine and whatever it's powering, and this paper documents that interface for the burner line's direct-DC output — the power-quality and conditioning questions that come with skipping a thermal cycle.
